title: Xavier to Asia
hookLine: Francis Xavier sails to India, Japan, and dies on an island off China
carry: to the ends of the earth

lines: A HUT ON AN ISLAND OFF CHINA.
A STUDENT IN PARIS, LONG BEFORE.
cards: So close he can see it. In a rough hut on a small island off China, a man lies with a fever. Across the water is the mainland he has been trying to reach.
Foreigners are not allowed in, and he is waiting for a trader who promised to smuggle him across. The trader doesn't come. He dies there, still looking at the shore.
Long before, he had been a proud young student in Paris, sharing lodgings with an older man who walked with a limp.

teach.h: A STUDENT WON OVER BY IGNATIUS.
teach.b: The man with the limp was Ignatius.

Francis Xavier was a gifted young Basque with plans for a fine career, and Ignatius, tradition says, kept asking him the question from the Gospel: "what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?"
Xavier joined him, and became one of the founding Jesuits.
Then, the story goes, when the man chosen to go east fell ill, Xavier was sent in his place, almost overnight. He sailed from Portugal, around Africa, to Goa in India.
He walked the fishing villages of the southern coast, and with helpers put prayers and teachings into the local language. Accounts say he rang a small bell in the streets to call children to learn.
In Japan he had to change his ways: learn courtesy, dress for respect, argue patiently with people who asked hard questions. Then he set his heart on China, and got as far as that island.
In Acts, Paul and Barnabas quote the Lord's command to be "for salvation unto the ends of the earth." Xavier took that line literally. There's a harder side too.
He traveled on the ships of an empire, and mission and empire were tangled in ways Christians in Asia, and historians, still talk about. Catholics honor him as a saint and a patron of missions.

teach.h: INDIA, JAPAN, AND THE CHINA COAST.
teach.b: And he was not the first Christian in India: the Thomas Christians of the southwest coast trace their church to the apostle Thomas, long before any Portuguese ship.
Asian Christians tell their own stories, which carried on long after the visitor was gone.

how: Catholics honor Francis Xavier as a saint and a patron of missions, and in Goa, India, his remains are kept and venerated; Christians in Asia remember him as part of the longer story of their churches.

games.q: you're Xavier, a gifted young student in Paris with plans for a fine career. an older man with a limp keeps asking what it profits to gain the whole world. what do you do?
o: laugh it off and keep your plans.
join him, and end up sent across the world.
games.why: he joins Ignatius, becomes one of the founding Jesuits, and is sent east, almost overnight.

practice: Picture a map and let your attention travel east the way Xavier's ship did: the fishing villages of India, the islands of Japan, the long shore of China.
Then let it fill with people you know there, or whose families come from there. If you pray, pray for them and for the churches and peoples of Asia; if you don't, wish them well, one by one.
